verdicts.evidence: A real divergence at function level, measured by extracting both forms: trivialReason("  because  ") = true shipped / false mutated (untrimmed: length 11 >= 8, and the brackets test is unanchored by the whitespace; the Set removes the \s itself). But the function is NOT exported and its only call site is conformance.js:415 on row.evidence, and parseManifest trims every cell before the row exists (cols = inner.split("|").map(c => c.replace(/`/g, "").trim()), and a multi-pipe evidence is rejoined from trimmed pieces with " | "): no evidence can carry leading or trailing whitespace. Sensitivity control run through the real CLI: mission examples/request-triage with the cell `|   because   |` (fixture .probe-5/fx/g-pad) -> exit 1 and the SAME violation line in both builds. The neighbouring divergent input (a cell with surrounding whitespace) is destroyed by the parser before reaching the function — impossible here.

verdicts.evidence: Realistic false red. Recipe: examples/request-triage, a single row of architecture.md changed to `| hexa-typescript-native | n/a | language locked at floor kickoff [ADR-0004] |` (fixture .probe-5/fx/g-brack-end); `check --strict` measured: shipped exit 0, mutated exit 1 + "n/a with an empty or placeholder reason". Without ^, any legitimate reason ENDING with a citation in brackets matches the placeholder pattern. The refusals that held still hold (g-pad, g-degen: identical exit 1). Why nothing sees it: the net (smoke line 193) only tests the fully bracketed placeholder `[reason]`, which both forms match; self-gate replayed with the mutated build: exit 0 (no n/a reason in the repository or the example ends with "]"); the other legs do not touch trivialReason.

verdicts.evidence: The bound of the lexical-degeneracy fix is not pinned. Recipe: n/a reason `test test` (9 characters, exactly 3 distinct characters t/e/s — the floor the code comment declares: "Three distinct characters is the floor"); fixture .probe-5/fx/g-three, measured: shipped exit 0, mutated exit 1 + placeholder violation. The fix's red side holds in both builds (`aaaa aaa aa`: identical exit 1, measured — fixture requested g-degen), but NO test of the net holds the green side of the bound, so < against <= is invisible. Self-gate replayed on the mutant: exit 0 (every real reason in the repository has well over 3 distinct characters); smoke/corpus have no reason with 3 distinct characters. What the net keeps of the fix: only its refusal side, not its boundary.

verdicts.evidence: Not equivalent, contrary to intuition: case folding is not bijective in Unicode. Measured mechanism: "ßxs ßxs ßxs".toLowerCase() -> Set {ß,x,s} of size 3 (passes); .toUpperCase() -> "SSXS..." because "ß" becomes "SS", Set {S,X} of size 2 (trivial). CLI recipe: this reason as n/a (fixture .probe-5/fx/g-eszett), measured: shipped exit 0, mutated exit 1 + placeholder violation. Refusals that held intact (g-degen exit 1 on both sides). Filed as hole and not equivalent because the divergent input can be constructed in a real manifest (any character with non-bijective case: ß, ligatures) — I cannot argue impossibility; an honestly narrow footprint: confined to strings that are already nearly degenerate and contain such characters. Nothing sees it: no fixture of the net has non-ASCII in an n/a reason; self-gate replayed on the mutant: exit 0.
